issuer_market_context: US-listed foreign issuer; operating company centered in Taiwan
authority_note: Additive research checkpoint only. companies/TSM/latest.json, registry/companies.json, reviews/latest.json, canonical raw-data, baseline-lock and frozen deterministic outputs remain unchanged; current canonical authority remains the 2026-09-06-deep run until a separate reviewed promotion.
portfolio_context: Actual holding, tax basis and portfolio risk budget were not supplied in this run. No position size is invented and buy authorization remains false.
structural_thesis: TSMC remains the dominant economic bottleneck in leading-edge foundry and advanced-node manufacturing for AI/HPC. Q2 2026 advanced-node mix reached 77% of wafer revenue, HPC reached 66% of revenue, 2nm contributed its first 3% of wafer revenue, and August monthly revenue reached a record NT$514.8B. The moat is strengthening operationally, but geographic concentration and a rapidly expanding global capital base mean shareholder returns depend on converting technical leadership into high post-expansion incremental returns.
current_finding: Harness-rule TTM diagnostics are approximately NT$4.440T revenue, NT$2.237T parent-attributable net income, NT$2.635T operating cash flow and NT$1.491T disclosed PPE purchases. Mechanical OCF-minus-PPE is approximately NT$1.144T. This is a diagnostic only, not normalized owner FCF, because TSMC is in an unusually intense N2/A14, advanced-packaging and overseas-fab investment cycle and working-capital, subsidy and lifecycle economics are not fully normalized.
economic_finding: Q2 2026 revenue was NT$1.270T, up 36% YoY, parent net income NT$706.6B, gross margin 67.7% and operating margin 60.3%. HPC represented 66% of Q2 revenue and 2nm already represented 3% of wafer revenue. Official August revenue was NT$514.8B, up 53.3% YoY; January-August revenue rose 39.3%. Independent foundry data placed TSMC at roughly 72.5% Q2 foundry share. These are strong widening-moat observations, not guarantees of future returns.
capital_and_survival: Financial survivability remains very strong, but capital intensity is rising materially. Management raised 2026 capex to US$60-64B and has committed to a much larger multiyear overseas footprint, including a US$265B Arizona investment plan. Overseas fabs and new nodes carry known gross-margin dilution and higher cost structures, so historical company-level returns cannot simply be applied to new capital cohorts.
permanent_loss_case: AI/HPC infrastructure returns disappoint and accelerator customers slow orders while TSMC continues heavy N2/A14, packaging and overseas capex; Samsung, Intel Foundry or alternative packaging ecosystems narrow the effective yield/cost gap in selected workloads; large customers use bargaining power to moderate pricing; Arizona/Japan fabs earn lower returns than Taiwan; and a Taiwan blockade, conflict or asset-access disruption makes ordinary solvency analysis irrelevant. The company can remain technologically excellent in non-catastrophic cases while shareholders suffer prolonged impairment through lower owner cash per ADS and multiple compression.
falsifiers: Leading-edge foundry share declines materially for multiple quarters while 2nm/A14 utilization or yield evidence weakens.
AI/HPC growth decelerates materially while capex remains elevated and OCF-PPE per ADS fails to improve through the cycle.
Overseas fabs show structurally lower after-tax incremental returns without sufficient pricing, subsidy or strategic-risk compensation.
The largest customers materially reduce roadmap dependence on TSMC or customer concentration rises while pricing power falls.
Gross and operating margins structurally erode beyond management's overseas-fab and new-node dilution framework.
Advanced-packaging constraints or competing packaging ecosystems cause customers to shift meaningful system value away from TSMC.
A Taiwan security event materially impairs production, asset access, cash repatriation or shareholder rights.
Capital requirements grow faster than revenue for a sustained period and after-tax incremental returns fall below the 9% hurdle.
Export controls or geopolitical fragmentation materially restrict TSMC's addressable leading-edge customer base.
The stock remains priced above conservative Base value while operating evidence weakens.
increase_evidence: N2/3nm and advanced-packaging demand remains strong beyond customer prebuild, with August/Q3 momentum converting into cash rather than inventory or receivable stress.
Arizona, Japan and other overseas capacity demonstrate competitive yield/utilization and after-tax incremental returns above the 9% hurdle despite disclosed margin dilution.
TTM OCF-PPE per ADS grows after the current capex wave begins to normalize; accounting profit growth alone is insufficient.
Top-customer concentration declines or the customer base broadens without sacrificing leading-edge pricing power and margins.
Overseas leading-edge capacity becomes economically and operationally substitutable for a meaningful subset of critical customer workloads, reducing Taiwan single-location tail risk.
N2 scales successfully and A14 customer adoption confirms continued process leadership without disproportionate capital destruction.
Expectation gap becomes clearly favorable through a materially lower price or materially higher normalized owner cash; price decline alone is insufficient.
sell_evidence: Sustained leading-edge share loss accompanied by weaker yields, pricing or customer migration.
AI/HPC demand weakens for multiple periods while capex remains structurally elevated.
Overseas-fab economics remain below the 9% hurdle after ramp and management continues accelerating capital commitments.
Gross-margin dilution materially exceeds expected overseas/new-node effects without offsetting strategic or cash returns.
One or two key customers materially reduce reliance on TSMC and the lost volume is not replaced at comparable economics.
OCF-PPE per ADS persistently lags revenue and earnings growth after the current expansion phase.
A material Taiwan disruption impairs production or shareholder access to cash/assets.
Export-control fragmentation or political constraints cause lasting leading-edge demand destruction.
Management sacrifices return discipline for politically motivated capacity that cannot earn the hurdle rate.
Valuation remains near bull economics while moat, cash or return-on-capital evidence deteriorates.

evidence: Q2 2026 advanced technologies represented 77% of wafer revenue; 2nm contributed its first 3% and HPC represented 66% of quarterly revenue.
Official August 2026 revenue reached NT$514.8B, up 53.3% YoY, and January-August revenue rose 39.3%.
counter_evidence: AI infrastructure demand is cyclical at the customer-capex level and current growth can contain prebuild ahead of capacity constraints or product transitions.

evidence: Q2 gross margin reached 67.7% while revenue grew 36% YoY, consistent with unusually strong customer value and pricing/yield economics.
TSMC serves the major advanced CPU, GPU, accelerator and custom-silicon ecosystems across multiple instruction sets and end customers.
counter_evidence: A small number of very large customers retain meaningful bargaining power and can redesign or dual-source across technology generations.
missing_data: Customer-level long-duration pricing and wallet-share data beyond public concentration disclosures.

evidence: Independent Q2 2026 foundry data placed TSMC at roughly 72.5% revenue share, while advanced-node utilization remained very high.
Successful 2nm first revenue, high advanced-node mix, packaging expansion and sustained margin strength indicate a widening process-plus-ecosystem moat.
counter_evidence: Samsung, Intel Foundry and alternative packaging ecosystems continue to invest, and overseas production can narrow TSMC's cost advantage even if technology leadership persists.

evidence: Harness-rule TTM parent net income is approximately NT$2.237T and mechanical OCF-PPE approximately NT$1.144T, showing very large absolute cash generation despite expansion.
Demand visibility remains strong enough for management to accelerate N2, packaging and overseas capacity.
counter_evidence: 2026 capex was raised to US$60-64B and management expects the next three years to be materially more capital intensive than the prior three.
Arizona and other overseas fabs carry structurally higher costs and management has disclosed gross-margin dilution from overseas fabs and new nodes.
missing_data: Cohort-level post-ramp after-tax returns for Arizona, Japan, N2/A14 and advanced packaging.

evidence: Management continues to allocate capital toward leading-edge nodes and packaging where customer roadmaps and utilization support demand, while preserving a strong balance sheet and dividends.
The geographic footprint is expanding to improve customer resilience and political optionality.
counter_evidence: US$265B of planned Arizona investment and broad geopolitical localization can pressure returns if capacity is built for strategic rather than economic reasons.
missing_data: Realized subsidy-adjusted return profile of the full overseas investment program.

evidence: Operating cash flow remains extremely strong relative to ordinary obligations and the company can internally finance a large share of current investment.
The existing harness model carries substantial liquidity and does not identify structural external-funding dependence.
counter_evidence: A Taiwan blockade or conflict is a non-financial survivability event that can overwhelm conventional liquidity analysis.

evidence: At the US$427.18 secondary September 10 reference, retained Base value of about US$309.90 is roughly 27% below price.
Holding retained Base economics requires approximately 15.01% annual revenue growth in years 2-10 at a 9% hurdle, implying year-10 revenue around US$651B.
counter_evidence: Management currently expects FY2026 revenue growth slightly above 40% in USD and previously outlined a roughly 25% company revenue CAGR framework through 2029, so the reverse growth is demanding but not demonstrably impossible.
missing_data: Normalized owner cash after the current global capex cycle.

evidence: Retained Bull value of about US$702 implies meaningful upside if AI/HPC and leading-edge economics remain exceptional.
counter_evidence: Retained Bear value is roughly 77% below the reference price, Base is roughly 27% below price, and catastrophic Taiwan risk is not fully represented by the normal Bear case.

evidence: The 2025 Form 20-F reported effective internal control over financial reporting and Deloitte issued unqualified opinions on both financial statements and ICFR; no material integrity failure was identified in reviewed evidence.
items.resolution_needed: Reassess on audit, ICFR, related-party or disclosure deterioration.

evidence: Large operating cash flow and liquidity support current investment without structural dependence on repeated outside financing.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor if global capex materially outruns internally generated cash for a sustained period.

evidence: No evidence reviewed establishes persistent excessive common-share dilution; the retained ADR denominator is based on the filing ordinary-share count divided by five.
items.resolution_needed: Continue monitoring ADS-equivalent share count and equity compensation.

evidence: Revenue growth is corroborated by advanced-node mix, HPC demand, record monthly revenue, high margins and strong operating cash flow rather than identified customer financing or subsidy-driven sales.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor receivables, inventory, customer prebuild and subsidy effects.

evidence: No collapse is proven, but 2026 capex of US$60-64B, a US$265B Arizona plan and higher-cost overseas fabs create very large new capital cohorts whose realized returns are not yet observable.
items.resolution_needed: Measure post-ramp utilization, yield, pricing, subsidy-adjusted invested capital and after-tax incremental returns versus the 9% hurdle.

evidence: Q2 foundry share, advanced-node mix, N2 launch and margin evidence point to a strengthening rather than shrinking moat.
items.resolution_needed: Track leading-edge share, yields, packaging share and customer migration.

evidence: The reference price requires approximately 15.01% annual revenue growth in years 2-10 under retained Base margin and terminal assumptions. This is demanding but below recent observed growth and management's medium-term growth framework, so it is not demonstrably a bull-only impossibility.
items.resolution_needed: Valuation remains unattractive even though this specific veto threshold is not crossed; require a larger expectation gap.

evidence: The top ten customers represented 78% of 2025 revenue and the two largest customers represented 19% and 17%. Manufacturing and the most advanced R&D ecosystem also remain heavily Taiwan-centered despite overseas diversification.
items.resolution_needed: Require broader customer economics and materially more substitutable overseas leading-edge capacity before treating concentration as non-fatal.

evidence: Conventional insolvency risk is low, but Taiwan geopolitical tail risk plus a valuation above retained Base and a historically large capex cycle can cause permanent or multi-year impairment.
items.resolution_needed: Reduce geographic tail risk, validate new-capital returns and establish a materially better expectation gap.

attacks: AI infrastructure overbuild causes accelerator customers to cut capex and leading-edge wafer demand.
Top customers use scale to pressure pricing or diversify meaningful volume to Samsung, Intel Foundry or internal alternatives.
N2/A14 process complexity raises tool and depreciation costs faster than pricing and yield improvements.
CoWoS and advanced-packaging bottlenecks become a constraint or competing packaging ecosystems capture more system value.
Arizona and Japan fabs operate at structurally lower margins and fail to earn the 9% hurdle after subsidies.
Political localization commitments cause overcapacity or capital allocation driven by policy rather than economics.
US labor, construction and infrastructure constraints delay Arizona ramps or increase unit costs.
Taiwan blockade, conflict or coercion disrupts production, logistics, asset access or cash distributions.
Export controls and geopolitical fragmentation reduce leading-edge demand from important regions or customers.
A 30x-plus translated earnings valuation compresses even if operational growth remains positive.

explicit_model_uncertainties: Post-ramp subsidy-adjusted ROIC of Arizona/Japan and new leading-edge capacity
Normalized owner cash after the current capex wave
Long-duration AI/HPC customer concentration and pricing
Economic substitutability of overseas fabs for Taiwan capacity
Probability and severity of Taiwan geopolitical disruption
